title: At a local complete intersection point the conormal module is free of rank n minus the dimension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $S=P/I$ and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal. Assume there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that the localization $S_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $d=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ be the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then $d$ is an integer with $0\le d\le n$, and the localization $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ of the $S$-module $I/I^2$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of rank $n-d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), implication (1) => (4), with c = height(q') - height(q) = n - dim_q(S) as in its statement (Lemma 00P2 lemma-codimension, line 28270, and dim_x A^n = n, Lemma 00OT and lemma-dim-affine-space); proof: last paragraph of the proof of 00SC (regular sequence of length t in k[y]_{q''}, J/J^2 free, Lemma 00S6 lemma-conormal-module-localize)

proof.text:
(Setup.) Let $W=\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ and $\lambda:S	o S_g$ the localization map [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Since $\mathfrak q$ is prime and $g
otin\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak q\cap W=\emptyset$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1) $ ar{\mathfrak q}:=\mathfrak qS_g$ is a prime ideal of $S_g$ with $\lambda^{-1}( ar{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$, and by its part (2) the map $S_{\mathfrak q}	o(S_g)_{ ar{\mathfrak q}}$, $s/u\mapsto\lambda(s)/\lambda(u)$, is an isomorphism of $S$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. In particular $S_g
eq0$, so by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] (1) there are integers $m,t\ge0$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_t\in Q:=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $\alpha:T:=Q/J\xrightarrow{\sim}S_g$, $J=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$, with $\dim S_g=m-t$. Let $ eta:Q	o Q/J\xrightarrow{\alpha}S_g$; it is a surjective homomorphism of $k$-algebras with kernel $J$. Put $\mathfrak q''= eta^{-1}( ar{\mathfrak q})$, a prime ideal of $Q$ containing $J$, and $ ar{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak q''/J=\alpha^{-1}( ar{\mathfrak q})$, a prime ideal of $T$. Since $\alpha$ is an isomorphism, $T
eq0$ and $\dim T=\dim S_g=m-t$ (Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ being a homeomorphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), last paragraph ('Assume (1)'): 'Let S_g = k[y_1..y_m]/(f_1..f_t) be a presentation of S_g as a global complete intersection. Write J = (f_1..f_t). Let q'' be the prime corresponding to qS_g'; Definition 00S9 (definition-lci-field, line 35817)

proof.text: (The dimension at $\mathfrak q$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}S_g\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ induced by $\lambda$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], so it is a homeomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ onto an open subset $O\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$; it sends $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ to $\lambda^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$ (step 1), so $\mathfrak q\in O$. A homeomorphism maps open neighbourhoods of a point onto open neighbourhoods of its image and strict chains of irreducible closed subsets onto strict chains of the same length, so it preserves the Krull dimension at a point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]; with [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] for $O$ we get $d=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(O)=\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}(\operatorname{Spec}S_g)$. Likewise the homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}S_g\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ sends $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ to $\bar{\mathfrak p}$, so $d=\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(\operatorname{Spec}T)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-equidimensional] applied to $T=Q/(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ ($T\neq0$, $\dim T=m-t$ by step 1), $d=m-t$. So $d$ is an integer, and $d\ge0$ because the Krull dimension at a point of a nonempty space lies in $\{0,1,\dots,\infty\}$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), last paragraph ('Assume (1)'): 'Note that t = m - dim(S_g) = height(q'') - height(q), see Lemma 00P2 (lemma-codimension)'; the equidimensionality of S_g is the paragraph after Definition 00S9 (lines 35834-35849)

proof.text: (Regular sequence at $\mathfrak q''$.) Let $R=Q_{\mathfrak q''}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] (hypotheses: $T\neq0$, $\dim T=m-t$, $J\subseteq\mathfrak q''$, step 1) the images $f_1/1,\dots,f_t/1$ form a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; they generate the ideal $JR$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] the $R/JR$-module $JR/(JR)^2$ is free with basis the classes of $f_1/1,\dots,f_t/1$, so $JR/(JR)^2\cong(R/JR)^{\oplus t}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), last paragraph ('Assume (1)'): 'As seen in the proof of Lemma 00SB (and also above) the elements f_1..f_t form a regular sequence in the local ring k[y_1..y_m]_{q''}. By Lemma 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular) we see that (J/J^2)_q is free of rank t'

proof.text: (The conormal module of $\beta$ at $\bar{\mathfrak q}$.) Let $U=Q\setminus\mathfrak q''$. Localizing at $U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] the exact sequences of $Q$-modules $0\to J\to Q\to T\to0$ and $0\to J^2\to J\to J/J^2\to0$ gives exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]: $U^{-1}J\to R$ is injective with image $JR$, $U^{-1}(J^2)$ maps onto $J^2R=(JR)^2$ inside it, hence $U^{-1}(J/J^2)\cong JR/(JR)^2$ and $U^{-1}T\cong R/JR$, compatibly with the module structures. The $S_g$-module structure of $J/J^2$ is the one through $\alpha:Q/J\cong S_g$, and since $\beta$ is surjective with $\beta^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q''$ we have $\beta(U)=S_g\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}$; so the localization of the $S_g$-module $J/J^2$ at $S_g\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}$ is $U^{-1}(J/J^2)$ (the same fractions $x/u$ and the same relation $u'(u_2x_1-u_1x_2)=0$, an element $u\in U$ acting as $\beta(u)$), and $U^{-1}T=T_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\cong(S_g)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$ by $\alpha$ and step 1. By step 3, $(J/J^2)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ is a free $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module of rank $t$: $(J/J^2)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus t}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), last paragraph ('Assume (1)'): '(J/J^2)_q is free of rank t' (the identification of the localization of J/J^2 with the conormal module of JR in k[y]_{q''}, left implicit in the source); localization is exact, Proposition 00CS (proposition-localization-exact, line 1336)

proof.text: (Comparison of the two presentations.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conormal-module-principal-localization] with the ring $k$, the $k$-algebra $S$, the element $g$, the presentation $\alpha_0:P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S=P/I$ (the quotient map, kernel $I$) and the presentation $\beta:k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to S_g$ of step 1 (kernel $J$): $(I/I^2)_g\oplus S_g^{\oplus m}\cong J/J^2\oplus S_g^{\oplus n}$ as $S_g$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Localize at $S_g\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; localization takes isomorphisms to isomorphisms and finite direct sums to direct sums, and $(S_g)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 1). For the $S$-module $M=I/I^2$ the map $M_{\mathfrak q}\to(M_g)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, $x/u\mapsto(x/1)/(u/1)$, is an isomorphism compatible with $S_{\mathfrak q}\cong(S_g)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$: every element of $(M_g)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ is $(x/g^a)/(s/g^b)=(g^bx/1)/(g^as/1)$ with $g^as\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, and $(x/1)/(u/1)=0$ means $(s/g^b)(x/1)=0$ in $M_g$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak q$, i.e. $g^csx=0$ with $g^cs\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, i.e. $x/u=0$ (this is the argument of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (2) for the module $M$). With step 4 we obtain an isomorphism of $S_{\mathfrak q}$-modules $N\oplus S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus m}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus(t+n)}$, where $N=(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), last paragraph ('Assume (1)'): 'By Lemma 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize, line 35776) we have J/J^2 (+) S_g^n = (I/I^2)_g (+) S_g^m'

proof.text: (Freeness and rank; conclusion.) By step 5, $N$ is a direct summand of the free $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module $S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus(t+n)}$, hence projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], hence flat [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]; it is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], being the image of $S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus(t+n)}$ under the projection onto the summand. The ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so $N$ is free [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free]. Tensoring $N\oplus S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus m}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus(t+n)}$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ shows that $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\otimes N$ has dimension $r:=t+n-m$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, so a basis of $N$ has exactly $r$ elements and $r\ge0$: $N\cong S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus r}$. By step 2, $r=n-(m-t)=n-d$. Hence $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ is free of rank $n-d$, and $n-d=r\ge0$ gives $d\le n$; with step 2, $0\le d\le n$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), last paragraph ('Assume (1)'): 'Thus (I/I^2)_q is free of rank t + n - m = m - dim(S_g) + n - m = n - dim(S_g) = height(q') - height(q) = c'; a finitely generated flat module over a local ring is free, Lemma 00NZ (lemma-finite-flat-local, line 19223)

split_report.summary: Proof written in 6 steps following the last paragraph of the proof of Stacks 00SC ((1) => (4)). Statement and stmt_deps kept. Steps: (1) the prime qS_g, S_q = (S_g)_{qS_g}, and the global complete intersection presentation beta: k[y_1..y_m] -> S_g with kernel J=(f_1..f_t), dim S_g = m - t; (2) d = dim_q Spec S = m - t via the open immersion Spec S_g -> Spec S, the open-subspace lemma and the new node for equidimensionality of a global complete intersection (paragraph after 00S9; the source writes this as 't = m - dim(S_g) = height(q'') - height(q)' via 00P2); (3) f_i regular sequence in k[y]_{q''} (new node, proof of 00SB as cited in 00SC) and J/J^2 of a regular sequence free (new node, 00LN in degree 1); (4) identification of (J/J^2)_{qS_g} with JR/(JR)^2 by exactness of localization (implicit in the source); (5) Lemma 00S6 (new node) localized at q; (6) the direct summand of a finite free module over the local ring S_q is free (existing Mathlib leaves 00NZ and projective => flat), rank t + n - m = n - d, which also gives d <= n. Four new unsplit nodes, each with leansearch, leanfinder/loogle and grep recorded; none in Mathlib (Mathlib has no quasi-regular sequences, no Cohen-Macaulay rings, no comparison of conormal modules of arbitrary presentations; Algebra.Generators.cotangentCompLocalizationAwayEquiv is only 08JZ (1)).

reviewed.note: 6 steps following the last paragraph of Stacks 00SC (1)=>(4): the prime of S_g and its localization; d = m - t via the open immersion Spec S_g -> Spec S and the equidimensionality of global complete intersections (new unsplit node, Section 00S8); the f_i form a regular sequence in k[y]_{q''} (new unsplit node from the proof of 00SB) and J/J^2 is free on them (new unsplit 00LN (1) node); localization of the conormal module; the comparison (I/I^2)_g + S_g^m = J/J^2 + S_g^n (new unsplit 00S6 node); a direct summand of a finite free module over the local ring S_q is free, of rank t + n - m = n - d >= 0. L checked the two new statements on the source: all components of a global complete intersection have dimension m - t, and t elements generating an ideal of height t in a Cohen-Macaulay local ring form a regular sequence.

lean.statement: theorem exists_basis_cotangent_localization_of_completeIntersection {k : Type u} [Field k] (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (q : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I)) (hci : ∃ g : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I, g ∉ q.asIdeal ∧ Algebra.IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g)) : ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDimAt q = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ d ≤ n ∧ Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin (n - d)) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl I.Cotangent))
